entries.subject: Bruce Van Natta
entries.summary: Diesel mechanic crushed by a 4.5-tonne truck axle in 2006 Wisconsin. Five major arteries severed. Reports seeing two angels with hands beneath the truck. Survives. Months later, his small intestine has tripled in length with no medical explanation.

entries.subject: Annabel Beam
entries.summary: Nine-year-old Texas girl with rare incurable digestive disorder (pseudo-obstruction motility disorder). Falls 30 feet straight down inside a hollow cottonwood tree. Unconscious for 5 hours during the rescue. Reports visiting heaven and meeting Jesus. Comes out uninjured — and her documented digestive disorder is gone. Specialist Dr. Samuel Nurko at Boston Children's confirms the inexplicable disappearance.

entries.subject: Don Piper
entries.summary: Texas pastor returning from a conference in January 1989. An eighteen-wheeler crosses the centerline head-on. Paramedics declare him dead at the scene — no pulse, no breathing, ninety minutes. Another pastor named Dick Onerecker stops at the wreckage, climbs into the crushed car, and prays over the body. Don begins to sing along with the hymn Dick prays.

entries.subject: Maximilian Kolbe
entries.summary: Auschwitz, July 1941. A prisoner escapes; the punishment is ten random men selected to die by starvation. The tenth man, Franciszek Gajowniczek, cries out for his wife and children. A Polish Franciscan priest steps forward — 'I am a Catholic priest, let me take his place.' The commander allows it. Two weeks later Kolbe is killed by lethal injection. Gajowniczek lives another fifty-three years and attends Kolbe's canonization in 1982.

entries.subject: The 33 Chilean Miners
entries.summary: San José Mine, Chile, August 2010. Thirty-three miners trapped seven hundred metres underground after a copper-and-gold mine collapse. José Henríquez emerges as the spiritual leader — leading twice-daily prayer for the sixty-nine days they wait. By the time the rescue capsule reaches them, all 33 are alive; 22 have committed their lives to faith. The world watches the rescue live.

entries.subject: Helen Roseveare
entries.summary: Eastern Congo, 1970s. British medical missionary delivers a premature baby; the mother dies, the only hot water bottle in the hospital bursts. A young African girl named Ruth prays simply: please send a hot water bottle today, and a doll for the baby's sister. That afternoon a parcel arrives — shipped from England five months earlier — containing exactly that.

entries.subject: Eben Alexander
entries.summary: Harvard-trained neurosurgeon contracts severe E. coli bacterial meningitis. Falls into a 7-day coma in 2008 Lynchburg Virginia. Reports an extended near-death experience — celestial realm, divine intelligence, meeting his deceased biological sister whom he'd never met. He was adopted; only saw her photo after recovering. Wrote *Proof of Heaven* in 2012.

entries.subject: Brother Andrew
entries.summary: Romanian border, 1955. Dutch missionary in his late twenties drives a baby-blue Volkswagen Beetle through the Iron Curtain, the back filled with Bibles for the underground church. At the border he prays a single sentence: make seeing eyes blind, do not let the guards see what you do not want them to see. The guards wave him through. He repeats the journey for thirty years and founds Open Doors.

entries.subject: Howard Storm
entries.summary: Paris, June 1985. Cincinnati art professor and committed atheist suffers a perforated stomach on a museum trip. Doctors leave him untreated overnight. He has a near-death experience that begins dark — dragged toward malevolent figures — until he cries the name of Jesus and is lifted into divine light. Resigns his university post. Becomes an ordained pastor.

entries.subject: Nicky Cruz
entries.tagline: every piece would still love you
entries.summary: Brooklyn, 1958. Mau Maus gang warlord, raised in Puerto Rico in a home of practising spiritualism, runs the most feared street gang in New York. Encounters David Wilkerson on a street corner: a thin Pennsylvania preacher who says 'Jesus loves you.' Cruz threatens to kill him; Wilkerson replies, 'You could cut me in a thousand pieces and lay them in the street, and every piece would still love you.' Cruz converts within months.

entries.subject: Asia Bibi
entries.summary: Punjab, Pakistan, June 2009. Christian farmworker, mother of five, drinks from a well in 102°F heat. Muslim co-workers refuse to drink after her — she's 'unclean.' The argument escalates; days later she's accused of blasphemy under Pakistan's 295-C law. Sentenced to death November 2010. Spends eight years on death row. October 2018, the Pakistani Supreme Court acquits her unanimously.

entries.subject: Lee Strobel
entries.summary: Chicago, 1981. Atheist legal-affairs editor at the *Chicago Tribune*, Yale Law–trained. His wife Leslie converts to Christianity; he sets out to prove the resurrection a hoax — interviewing thirteen scholars over two years to demolish the case. On November 8, 1981, after compiling the evidence against himself, he reverses position and converts. *The Case for Christ* (1998) reconstructs the investigation.
